paragraphs.title: The Fall of Babylon and Israel’s Return

easy.explanation: The word of the LORD was spoken against Babylon and the land of the Chaldeans.
easy.q: Against which land was the prophecy spoken?

easy.explanation: Bel was confounded, Merodach was broken, and Babylon’s images were broken in pieces.
easy.q: What happened to Babylon’s idols?

easy.explanation: The children of Israel and Judah would come together to seek the LORD.
easy.q: Who would come together seeking the LORD?

medium.explanation: A nation from the north would come against Babylon and make her land desolate.
medium.q: What would make Babylon’s land desolate?

answers: The LORD and the way to Zion
medium.explanation: They would ask the way to Zion and seek the LORD their God.
medium.q: What would Israel and Judah seek on their return?

answers: Let us depart from the LORD
Let us unite ourselves to the LORD
Let us fight against the LORD
medium.explanation: The phrase describes joining themselves to the LORD in a perpetual covenant.
medium.q: What does “let us join ourselves to the LORD” mean?

answers: A turning from idols to seeking the LORD
A change from war to trade
A return to rule over Babylon
challenge.explanation: The people leave their former condition and seek the LORD and Zion.
challenge.q: What spiritual change is described in this passage?

answers: Both are part of the LORD’s announced work
challenge.explanation: The judgment of Babylon is presented alongside the return of Israel and Judah.
challenge.q: How are Babylon’s fall and Israel’s return related?

answers: Israel and Judah would return in unity
challenge.explanation: The verse specifically says that Israel and Judah would come together.
challenge.q: What does the word “together” emphasize?

easy.explanation: An assembly of great nations would come from the north country.
easy.q: From which direction would the nations come against Babylon?

easy.explanation: Chaldea would be taken as spoil, and Babylon would be captured.
easy.q: What would the conquerors do to Babylon?

easy.explanation: They would turn every one to his own people and flee to his own land.
easy.q: What would the peoples of the empire do after Babylon fell?

medium.explanation: The comparison describes arrows used by a mighty and practiced warrior.
medium.q: What does “as of a mighty expert man” show about the army?

medium.explanation: The fallen foundations and walls represent the collapse of Babylon’s power.
medium.q: What was the result of Babylon’s fallen walls and foundations?

medium.explanation: Spoil is property seized from the defeated.
medium.q: What does “spoil” mean in this passage?

answers: Many nations surrounding and taking Babylon
challenge.explanation: An assembly of great nations is arranged against Babylon and takes her.
challenge.q: What overall picture is given of the invading army?

challenge.explanation: The command tells the archers to continue the attack and show no restraint.
challenge.q: What does “spare no arrows” command the attackers to do?

answers: Israel sinned and Babylon was spared
challenge.explanation: The passage says, “she hath sinned against the LORD.”
challenge.q: What cause of Babylon’s judgment is stated?

paragraphs.title: Babylon’s Punishment and the Promise of Israel’s Restoration

easy.explanation: Israel is called a scattered sheep.
easy.q: To what is Israel compared?

easy.explanation: The king of Assyria is named as the first who devoured Israel.
easy.q: Who first devoured Israel?

answers: Bring Israel again to his habitation
easy.explanation: The LORD promised to bring Israel again to his habitation.
easy.q: What did the LORD promise to do for Israel?

answers: It was the last lion to attack Israel
medium.explanation: Babylon, like the last lion, had broken Israel’s bones and would be punished.
medium.q: Why would Babylon be punished according to the passage?

answers: Babylon would be punished as Assyria was
Assyria would be punished instead of Babylon
medium.explanation: The LORD would punish Babylon as he had punished the king of Assyria.
medium.q: What comparison is made between Assyria and Babylon?

answers: Those who remain as a remnant
medium.explanation: The phrase refers to those whom the LORD preserves after judgment.
medium.q: What does “whom I reserve” refer to?

answers: Babylon is punished while Israel is restored
Babylon returns to Zion while Israel remains captive
challenge.explanation: Babylon receives judgment, while Israel is promised restoration and pardon.
challenge.q: What contrast is made between Babylon and Israel?

answers: The LORD will pardon the remnant
The sins will be transferred to Babylon
challenge.explanation: The passage connects the absence of sin with the LORD’s pardon.
challenge.q: What does it mean that Israel’s iniquity and Judah’s sins shall not be found?

answers: Tyre, Sidon, and the Red Sea
challenge.explanation: The LORD says Israel shall feed on Carmel and Bashan and be satisfied in Ephraim and Gilead.
challenge.q: Which places represent the abundance awaiting restored Israel?

paragraphs.title: The Destruction of Babylon’s Allied Lands

easy.explanation: The LORD commanded the conqueror to waste and utterly destroy the land.
easy.q: What was the conqueror commanded to do to the land?

answers: The hammer of the whole earth
easy.explanation: Babylon is called “the hammer of the whole earth.”
easy.q: What was Babylon called?

easy.explanation: Those who fled would go to Zion to declare the vengeance of the LORD and his temple.
easy.q: Where would those who escaped Babylon go to declare the LORD’s vengeance?

medium.explanation: The hammer image emphasizes Babylon’s former strength and dominance.
medium.q: What does the image “the hammer of the whole earth” emphasize?

answers: So that nothing would be left of her
medium.explanation: The command says, “let nothing of her be left.”
medium.q: Why was Babylon to be destroyed utterly?

answers: Judgment for the harm done to the LORD’s temple
Building a new temple in Babylon
medium.explanation: The phrase refers to the LORD’s vengeance for the wrong done against his temple.
medium.q: What is meant by “the vengeance of his temple”?

answers: The hammer of the earth becomes broken and desolate
challenge.explanation: Babylon, once powerful, is shown cut asunder, broken, and desolate.
challenge.q: What change is described in Babylon’s condition?

answers: They carried the report of vengeance to Zion
challenge.explanation: They escaped from Babylon to declare the LORD’s vengeance in Zion.
challenge.q: What role did the fugitives and escaped people have?

answers: It is repayment for its opposition to the LORD
Its actions save it from judgment
challenge.explanation: Babylon is judged because it strove against the LORD and harmed his heritage and temple.
challenge.q: How is Babylon’s destruction connected with its actions?

easy.explanation: The archers were commanded to camp against Babylon round about.
easy.q: What were the nations called to do to Babylon?

answers: They would go up to Zion
easy.explanation: Babylon’s young men would fall, and its men of war would be cut off.
easy.q: What would happen to Babylon’s young men and warriors?

easy.explanation: The LORD of hosts is called Israel’s strong Redeemer.
easy.q: Who is Israel’s Redeemer?

answers: Babylon would be repaid according to its deeds
Babylon would be rewarded for its deeds
Israel would pay for Babylon’s deeds
medium.explanation: The nations are told to recompense Babylon according to all that she had done.
medium.q: What principle of justice appears in the passage?

medium.explanation: The most proud would stumble and fall, and none would raise him up.
medium.q: What would happen to Babylon’s pride?

medium.explanation: Babylon’s pride describes arrogant and defiant behavior.
medium.q: What does “proud” mean in this context?

answers: The LORD judges Babylon and gives rest to the land
challenge.explanation: The LORD pleads Israel’s cause while bringing rest to the land and trouble to Babylon.
challenge.q: How are Babylon’s judgment and Israel’s redemption connected?

answers: The LORD can defend Israel and plead its cause
challenge.explanation: The title emphasizes the LORD’s power to redeem and defend his people.
challenge.q: What does the title “strong Redeemer” emphasize?

answers: The LORD kindles a fire in her cities
challenge.explanation: After the proud one falls, the LORD kindles a fire in Babylon’s cities.
challenge.q: What follows the fall of Babylon’s pride?

paragraphs.title: The Sword Against Every Babylonian Power

answers: The Chaldeans and Babylon’s leaders and forces
easy.explanation: The sword is named against the Chaldeans, Babylon’s inhabitants, princes, wise men, and mighty men.
easy.q: Against whom would the sword come?

easy.explanation: The passage says, “A drought is upon her waters; and they shall be dried up.”
easy.q: What would happen to Babylon’s waters?

easy.explanation: Wild beasts of the desert, wild beasts of the islands, and owls would dwell there.
easy.q: Who would dwell in Babylon’s ruins?

answers: To show that every part of Babylon’s power would suffer
To show that only the army would suffer
medium.explanation: The sword reaches leaders, soldiers, horses, chariots, treasures, and waters.
medium.q: Why is the sword described as affecting so many areas?

answers: Babylon’s desolation is linked with its graven images
medium.explanation: The drought is mentioned alongside the statement that Babylon is a land of graven images.
medium.q: What connection is made between the dried waters and Babylon’s idols?

medium.explanation: The phrase refers to animals that inhabit deserted and desolate places.
medium.q: What are “wild beasts of the desert”?

answers: It changes from a rich power into a dry and desolate place
It changes from a desert into a flourishing city
It changes from a weak kingdom into an empire
challenge.explanation: The sword strikes its people and wealth, its waters dry up, and wild creatures inhabit it.
challenge.q: What complete change is described for Babylon?

answers: The judgment reaches society, armies, wealth, and resources
The judgment is limited to the palace
challenge.explanation: The list includes wise men, warriors, horses, chariots, treasures, and waters.
challenge.q: What does the list of those and things struck by the sword reveal?

answers: Its idolatry is associated with shame and desolation
The passage does not mention idols
challenge.explanation: Babylon is called a land of graven images before its desolation is described.
challenge.q: How are Babylon’s idols related to its fate?

paragraphs.title: The Northern People and Babylon’s Fear

answers: A great people and many kings
easy.explanation: A great nation and many kings would come from the north and distant coasts.
easy.q: Who would come against Babylon?

easy.explanation: The invaders would hold the bow and the lance.
easy.q: What weapons would the invading people carry?

answers: His hands became weak and he was afraid
easy.explanation: His hands waxed feeble, and anguish and labor pains took hold of him.
easy.q: What happened to the king of Babylon when he heard the report?

answers: The danger was broad and organized
medium.explanation: Many kings indicate a large and coordinated threat.
medium.q: What does the presence of many kings show?

answers: The pangs of a woman in travail
medium.explanation: His fear is compared with the pangs of a woman in travail.
medium.q: To what is the king’s anguish compared?

answers: He lost courage and strength to act
medium.explanation: The expression describes fear, weakness, and loss of confidence.
medium.q: What does “his hands waxed feeble” mean?

answers: It breaks the confidence of Babylon’s king
challenge.explanation: The report alone causes the king’s hands to become weak and anguish to seize him.
challenge.q: Why is the report of the enemy dangerous even before the battle?

answers: The army is numerous, armed, and merciless
The army is weak and unprepared
The army is unrelated to his fear
challenge.explanation: The invaders are numerous, armed with bows and lances, and described as cruel.
challenge.q: How does the description of the army explain the king’s fear?

answers: It personifies Babylon as facing the invading army
It identifies a city unrelated to Babylon
challenge.explanation: The expression addresses Babylon as a personified city or kingdom.
challenge.q: What does “daughter of Babylon” do in the passage?

paragraphs.title: The Lord’s Counsel and the Final Desolation

easy.explanation: The enemy is compared to a lion coming from the swelling of Jordan.
easy.q: What animal represents the enemy coming against Babylon?

answers: No one can stand before him
easy.explanation: The LORD asks who the shepherd is that can stand before him, showing that none can resist him.
easy.q: Who can stand before the LORD?

answers: The earth was moved and the nations cried out
easy.explanation: At the noise of Babylon’s taking, the earth was moved and a cry was heard among the nations.
easy.q: What happened when Babylon was taken?

medium.explanation: The lion represents a powerful enemy advancing against Babylon.
medium.q: What does the lion image emphasize?

answers: It shows that Babylon’s destruction is part of the LORD’s purpose
medium.explanation: The LORD’s counsel and purposes determine what will happen to Babylon.
medium.q: What is the role of the LORD’s counsel?

medium.explanation: A habitation is a place where someone or something dwells.
medium.q: What does “habitation” mean in this context?

answers: Even the seemingly weak can overcome Babylon by the LORD’s purpose
They have no part in the judgment
challenge.explanation: Even the least of the flock will draw Babylon out and make its habitation desolate.
challenge.q: What does “the least of the flock” suggest about the agents of judgment?

answers: It moves the earth and causes a cry among the nations
challenge.explanation: The passage says the earth is moved and the cry is heard among the nations.
challenge.q: How does Babylon’s fall affect the world beyond the city?

answers: No power can resist the LORD’s decision
Babylon’s king can challenge the LORD
The battle will have no result
challenge.explanation: The questions emphasize the LORD’s unmatched authority and Babylon’s inevitable fall.
challenge.q: What do the LORD’s questions about being like him and standing before him imply?
